sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，在这个播客里，我们探讨二十多岁时经历的一些重大生活变化和过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，很高兴你能回来收听新一期节目，我们将继续剖析二十多岁的心理。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about love.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要谈谈爱。

sentences.en: Love, meeting someone new, being obsessed with them is honestly one of the best feelings that I think we can experience.
sentences.zh: 爱，遇见某人，对他们着迷，老实说，我认为这是我们能体验到的最美好的感觉之一。

sentences.en: There is something special about those early days that is just so exciting and addictive.
sentences.zh: 那些早期的日子里有一种特别的东西，既令人兴奋又让人上瘾。

sentences.en: It feels like the honeymoon period is going to last forever.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像蜜月期会永远持续下去。

sentences.en: And then obviously, at some stage, real life kind of sets back in.
sentences.zh: 然后很明显，在某个阶段，现实生活会回归。

sentences.en: Or for some of us, that initial craziness is really, really terrifying.
sentences.zh: 或者对我们中的一些人来说，那种最初的疯狂真的非常非常可怕。

sentences.en: It's really scary to feel like this person who we may love might actually be a source of fear for us, not because they are unsafe,
sentences.zh: 感觉到我们所爱的人可能实际上是我们恐惧的来源，这真的很可怕，不是因为他们不安全，

sentences.en: but because what we are experiencing for the first time is healthy love.
sentences.zh: 而是因为我们第一次体验到的是健康的爱。

sentences.en: And that healthy love feels like boredom.
sentences.zh: 而那种健康的爱感觉就像无聊。

sentences.en: It can cause us to call into question all of these different things, whether this person is actually right for us.
sentences.zh: 它会让我们质疑所有这些不同的事情，质疑这个人是否真的适合我们。

sentences.en: And I really want to break that down today.
sentences.zh: 今天我真的想深入剖析这一点。

sentences.en: And that big question of why does healthy love sometimes feel boring?
sentences.zh: 关于“为什么健康的爱有时会让人感到无聊”这个大问题，

sentences.en: And does this sense of boredom truly mean that this person is not right for you?
sentences.zh: 这种无聊感是否真的意味着这个人不适合你？

sentences.en: Or is it just your relationship anxiety popping up at the worst time?
sentences.zh: 还是说这只是你的关系焦虑在最糟糕的时候冒了出来？

sentences.en: We are joined by the brilliant Sarah Yudkin for this episode from You Love and You Learn.
sentences.zh: 本期节目我们邀请到了《You Love and You Learn》的杰出嘉宾Sarah Yudkin。

sentences.en: I'm so excited to have her on because she speaks so much about relationship anxiety and the ways that it gets in our way of finding really fulfilling love and relationships.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能邀请她来，因为她谈论了很多关于关系焦虑的话题，以及它是如何阻碍我们找到真正令人满足的爱和关系的。

sentences.en: So Sarah, welcome.
sentences.zh: 那么Sarah，欢迎你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for coming on to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你来到这个播客。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: I'm excited to talk about this.
sentences.zh: 我很兴奋能谈论这个话题。

sentences.en: I feel like I can talk about it all day.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我可以谈论它一整天。

sentences.en: So buckle up.
sentences.zh: 所以系好安全带吧。

sentences.en: My goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Well, it's so interesting because you listened to an episode that we did around relationship anxiety with Katie and you were like, oh my goodness,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣，因为你听了我们之前关于Katie的关系焦虑那一期节目，当时你说，天哪，

sentences.en: this sounds exactly like what I talk about in my practice.
sentences.zh: 这听起来和我工作中谈论的内容一模一样。

sentences.en: And it's really not spoken about that much.
sentences.zh: 而且这确实没有被讨论得太多。

sentences.en: I don't think I even really came across it until I got into my most recent relationship and was like, why is this suddenly so hard yet so easy?
sentences.zh: 我想在我进入最近这段关系之前，我甚至没有真正遇到过这种情况，当时我就想，为什么这突然变得这么难，却又这么容易？

sentences.en: Like, I feel like that is such a much more common experience than we know.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这比我们想象的要普遍得多。

sentences.en: Before I jump into it though, I feel like I'm just jumping the gun.
sentences.zh: 不过在深入探讨之前，我觉得我有点操之过急了。

sentences.en: Kat, are you able to like briefly introduce yourself, tell us about who you are, about your work?
sentences.zh: Kat，你能简单介绍一下自己，告诉我们你是谁，以及你的工作吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So I'm Sarah and I help people who are in healthy, loving relationships.
sentences.zh: 我是Sarah，我帮助那些处于健康、充满爱的关系中的人们。

sentences.en: I always give that disclaimer right from the jump that we're not talking about abuse here, but I help people who are in healthy, loving relationships,
sentences.zh: 我总是从一开始就给出免责声明，我们这里讨论的不是虐待，但我帮助那些处于健康、充满爱的关系中，

sentences.en: but also who have anxiety that's holding them back.
sentences.zh: 但同时又被焦虑所困扰的人。

sentences.en: And the reason why I fell into this work is because my parents got a divorce actually when I was in my 20s.
sentences.zh: 我之所以从事这项工作，是因为我二十多岁时父母离婚了。

sentences.en: And at the time I kind of stuffed it down and was like, it's okay, I get why they did it.
sentences.zh: 当时我把它压抑下去了，心想，没关系，我理解他们为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: They're better off, they're happier.
sentences.zh: 他们分开会更好，会更快乐。

sentences.en: And I thought that I didn't necessarily care that much.
sentences.zh: 我以为我并不怎么在意。

sentences.en: I was like, it is what it is.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: But when I found myself in a very safe, loving relationship, I very quickly realized that the fear of divorce kind of was looming in the background.
sentences.zh: 但当我发现自己处于一段非常安全、充满爱的关系中时，我很快意识到，离婚的恐惧在背景中隐隐作现。

sentences.en: And right when things started getting serious with now my fiance, but at the time my boyfriend,
sentences.zh: 就在我和现在的未婚夫，当时还是男朋友的关系变得认真时，

sentences.en: I was like, what if I got a divorce?
sentences.zh: 我心想，如果我也离婚了怎么办？

sentences.en: How do I know I'm not going to get a divorce?
sentences.zh: 我怎么知道我不会离婚？

sentences.en: How do I pick the perfect person and make sure that he has no red flags and that everything is exactly what I'm envisioning in order to make sure that this doesn't happen?
sentences.zh: 我该如何挑选完美的人，确保他没有任何危险信号，确保一切都如我所愿，以确保这种情况不会发生？

sentences.en: And I realized that it did affect me a lot more than I thought at the time.
sentences.zh: 我意识到它对我的影响比我当时想象的要大得多。

sentences.en: And maybe I hadn't fully processed the fears around love and relationships.
sentences.zh: 也许我还没有完全消化对爱和关系的恐惧。

sentences.en: And so I just became so fascinated by it.
sentences.zh: 所以我对此变得非常着迷。

sentences.en: And now I help others through their journey with that.
sentences.zh: 现在我帮助其他人走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: Oh my goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That's actually, congratulations on your engagement as well.
sentences.zh: 这真是，也祝贺你订婚。

sentences.en: That is so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 那太美好了。

sentences.en: And I think a story that is
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个

sentences.en: so much more commonplace than we think.
sentences.zh: 比我们想象中普遍得多的故事。

sentences.en: There are so many small things in our past, in our childhoods, even in our adolescence, in our twenties that really shape how we approach and see love.
sentences.zh: 在我们的过去、童年、青春期，甚至二十多岁时，有太多微小的事情真正塑造了我们看待和接近爱的方式。

sentences.en: And I think you can experience anxiety in any area of your life in which there is fear, any area of your life in which you have expectations or a false alarm.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以在生活的任何领域体验到焦虑，只要有恐惧存在，只要你有期望或虚惊一场的地方。

sentences.en: So can you kind of explain what relationship anxiety actually is?
sentences.zh: 那么你能解释一下什么是关系焦虑吗？

sentences.en: What kind of sets it apart from what we would typically see anxiety as being?
sentences.zh: 它与我们通常所见的焦虑有什么不同？

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So my take is that there's kind of like a, I don't even like the word normal, but I'm just going to use it here for this case.
sentences.zh: 我的看法是，有一种，我甚至不喜欢“正常”这个词，但我在这里就用它吧。

sentences.en: I think there's a normal amount of questions that could come up when you're committing to someone for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你决定与某人共度余生时，出现一定数量的问题是正常的。

sentences.en: Like, oh, is this someone I want to be with?
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，这是我想在一起的人吗？

sentences.en: Or, you know, kind of just like assessing the situation.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，只是评估一下情况。

sentences.en: Whereas relationship anxiety takes it up a notch to a whole nother level.
sentences.zh: 而关系焦虑则将其提升到了另一个层面。

sentences.en: And a question such as, is my partner funny enough, can turn into a three-week spiral because then it's not only are they funny enough, but oh my gosh,
sentences.zh: 像“我的伴侣够不够幽默”这样的问题，可能会演变成长达三周的恶性循环，因为那时不仅是他们够不够幽默，而是天哪，

sentences.en: I'm never going to laugh in my life.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子都不会再笑了。

sentences.en: And I'm going to wake up one day and realize that I could have married this other person that was funnier.
sentences.zh: 有一天我会醒来，意识到我本可以嫁给另一个更幽默的人。

sentences.en: And so relationship anxiety is doubt about your healthy relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以关系焦虑是对你健康关系的怀疑。

sentences.en: And again, I say the word healthy because if you're having anxiety because you're being mistreated, then that's not what we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 我再次强调“健康”这个词，因为如果你是因为被虐待而感到焦虑，那不是我们在这里讨论的内容。

sentences.en: But it's really taking up a notch the normal questioning or doubts that might come up in a relationship.
sentences.zh: 但它确实将关系中可能出现的正常质疑或怀疑提升了一个档次。

sentences.en: And it can come in the form of physical symptoms like your chest tightens, you have lurching stomach when you think about the future.
sentences.zh: 它可能以身体症状的形式出现，比如胸口紧绷，想到未来时胃部翻腾。

sentences.en: You feel maybe like warm or sweaty sometimes when you're trying to kind of sort out how to move forward in your relationship.
sentences.zh: 当你试图理清如何在关系中前进时，有时会感到发热或出汗。

sentences.en: Or it can come in the more mental symptoms like overthinking, waking up and kind of starting to initially ask questions about your relationship
sentences.zh: 或者它可能以更多的心理症状出现，比如过度思考，醒来后开始质疑你的关系，

sentences.en: or getting home after spending time with your partner and kind of fact-checking everything and having this microscope of, was that fun enough?
sentences.zh: 或者和伴侣待在一起后回到家，开始核对一切，用显微镜审视：那足够有趣吗？

sentences.en: Did I feel good enough?
sentences.zh: 我感觉足够好吗？

sentences.en: All of that.
sentences.zh: 所有这些。

sentences.en: So that's a little bit more about it, but I'm happy to explain anything else as far as how it comes up too.
sentences.zh: 这就是关于它的一些内容，我很乐意解释它如何出现的其他方面。

sentences.en: It's really interesting because all of those, I don't know if they're symptoms, but all of those, let's just call them feelings or indicators of relationship anxiety
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为所有这些，我不知道它们是否是症状，但所有这些，我们称之为关系焦虑的感觉或指标，

sentences.en: feel a lot like justified anxiety.
sentences.zh: 感觉起来很像是合理的焦虑。

sentences.en: Feel a lot like, not so much justified anxiety, but justified fears, right?
sentences.zh: 感觉起来，与其说是合理的焦虑，不如说是合理的恐惧，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I think the thing about anxiety of any form of particular relation, particularly relationship anxiety is that there is, it's very difficult to distinguish between,
sentences.zh: 我认为任何形式的焦虑，特别是关系焦虑，其特点在于很难区分：

sentences.en: is this actually a real fear or is this a false alarm?
sentences.zh: 这真的是一种真实的恐惧，还是虚惊一场？

sentences.en: And if I ignore what is a real fear, what are the consequences of that going to be?
sentences.zh: 如果我忽略了真实的恐惧，会有什么后果？

sentences.en: So I think that that hypervigilance also comes from like a place of like perfectionism as well, of like, I want to ensure that I make no mistakes when it comes to this,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种过度警觉也源于一种完美主义，即我想确保在这件事上我不犯任何错误，

sentences.en: that I'm not overlooking anything that could potentially harm me.
sentences.zh: 我没有忽略任何可能伤害我的事情。

sentences.en: And then I think it comes down to inevitably what is self-sabotage, where because you are so hypervigilant over every single minute detail of your relationship,
sentences.zh: 然后我认为这不可避免地归结为自我破坏，因为你对关系的每一个微小细节都过度警觉，

sentences.en: you don't actually give someone space to be imperfect or to be authentic or to maybe do things that you don't totally love and adore, but which are part of like our quirks.
sentences.zh: 你实际上没有给对方空间去变得不完美，去变得真实，或者去做一些你并不完全喜欢和崇拜，但却是我们怪癖一部分的事情。

sentences.en: Do you think that relationship anxiety causes us to self-sabotage a lot?
sentences.zh: 你认为关系焦虑会导致我们进行大量的自我破坏吗？

sentences.en: Definitely, definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会，绝对会。

sentences.en: And I want to circle back to one thing you just said, which is that it can be really hard to parse out what is your anxiety versus what is your fear.
sentences.zh: 我想回到你刚才说的一点，那就是很难区分什么是你的焦虑，什么是你的恐惧。

sentences.en: And I just want to remind people that love and relationships have a lot of risk associated with them, right?
sentences.zh: 我只想提醒大家，爱和关系本身就伴随着很多风险，对吧？

sentences.en: So no matter how happy you are in the relationship or no matter how safe or no matter how steady the relationship is, we don't get guarantees, right?
sentences.zh: 所以无论你在关系中多么快乐，无论关系多么安全或稳定，我们都没有保证，对吧？

sentences.en: Like we don't know what's going to happen in the future.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道未来会发生什么。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of potential loss or people have fear of abandonment, fear of failure.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多潜在的损失，或者人们有被遗弃的恐惧、失败的恐惧。

sentences.en: Like what does it mean if this doesn't work out and I put all of this energy into it?
